label: NI

notes.grounding: Measured behavior is exact: --min-percent lands in the positional branch as SPEC_FOLDER and 90 triggers 'ERROR: Unexpected argument: 90' with exit 1 (script lines 551-558). The 86% fixture arithmetic (3 placeholders over 21 content lines, bc scale=2, printf %.0f) gives 86. The exit-code footer (lines 589-591) and its '#   N - ' format are real. One wrong claim: the data flow treats the per-file percentage under --file as a variable the check can read after the report, but it is a local inside calculate_file_completeness and the output functions and lives only in the stats file.
notes.requirements: REQ-001 to REQ-005 are testable and cover exit 3 below N, exit 0 otherwise, unchanged output, and bad or missing values (exit 1). Nothing pins down the boundary case at exactly N, negative values, a flag token given as the value (e.g. --min-percent --json), or what happens under --file when the file is missing (the percentage falls back to 0).
notes.verification: Every task has a Verify clause with a command and an expected result, and the fixture is built and checked first. Gaps: no test at exactly N (e.g. --min-percent 86 on the 86% fixture), so an off-by-one using -le would pass every check. The text-report diff (T008) runs only on the passing 100% packet, never on the failing run. T005 checks exit 1 but not the error message REQ-001 requires. T008 diffs against a baseline taken in T003, which breaks if the packet's own docs change line counts in between.
notes.scope: Stays on the one option at Level 1. No invented subsystems, no unfilled tokens, no filler.
notes.consistency: The ids, the script path, exit codes 0, 1 and 3, the 86% fixture and the 100% packet all match across spec.md, plan.md and tasks.md.
notes.clarity: A developer could implement this. Two things are left implicit: where the check goes relative to the unconditional 'exit 0' at line 587, and that --file mode has to source the stats file to get the percentage.

defects: plan.md:63: says the check reads 'the per-file percentage under --file' as the same variable the report printed, but in the script percentage is local to calculate_file_completeness/output_text/output_json and exists only in the stats file, so no global is available after the report
spec.md:115: names '[[ =~ ]]' as a construct to keep compatible and says to reuse constructs the script already uses, but the script has no =~ anywhere
spec.md:85-86: no requirement or acceptance criterion for N exactly equal to the reported percentage, negative N, or a flag token given as the value
spec.md:125: --file mode is in scope but the missing-file case (the percentage falls back to 0, so the run would exit 3) is not addressed
tasks.md:54: T006 tests 90 and 50 on an 86% fixture but nothing at exactly 86, so an off-by-one comparison would pass
tasks.md:63: T008 diffs the text report only on the passing packet run, never on a failing (exit 3) run, though SC-001 (spec.md:102) asks for an unchanged report on the 86% fixture
tasks.md:53: T005 Verify checks only exit 1, not that an error is printed as REQ-001 requires
tasks.md:44,63: the T008 baseline comes from T003 on the packet folder itself, so any edit to the packet's spec/plan/tasks in between changes the line counts and breaks the diff
